message.content:
The volume \(V\) of a cone is given by

\[
V=\frac{1}{3}\pi r^{2}h
\]

where  
\(r = 3 \text{ cm}\) (base radius) and  
\(h = 5 \text{ cm}\) (height).

\[
\begin{aligned}
V &= \frac{1}{3}\pi (3)^2(5) \\
  &= \frac{1}{3}\pi (9)(5) \\
  &= \frac{1}{3}\pi (45) \\
  &= 15\pi \text{ cm}^3
\end{aligned}
\]

Numerically,

\[
15\pi \approx 15 \times 3.14159 \approx 47.12 \text{ cm}^3
\]

So the cone’s volume is **\(15\pi \text{ cm}^3\)** (about **47.1 cm³**).
